description.value: The study examined prosocial behavior, resting autonomic physiology, and structural brain correlates in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia.

spans.text: The results of the present study indicate that parasympathetic nervous system dysfunction relates to diminished prosocial behavior in bvFTD.

value: We hypothesized that prosocial behavior would be impaired in bvFTD, but not AD, compared to healthy controls and that prosocial helping deficits would relate to baseline parasympathetic dysfunction.
Neuroanatomically, we anticipated that salience network atrophy would be associated with prosocial behavior deficits in bvFTD.

Given the critical role of the left frontoinsula in parasympathetic activity, we also investigated whether left-lateralized frontoinsula atrophy was a common neural substrate underlying impairment in both RSA and prosociality in bvFTD.
